headline: Former OpenAI exec Ryan Beiermeister joins Founders Fund as partner
summary: Beiermeister previously served as VP of Product Policy at OpenAI
details: Ryan Beiermeister has joined Founders Fund as a partner. She previously spent about two years as VP of Product Policy at OpenAI.
Beiermeister was reportedly fired from OpenAI in February after objecting to a planned ChatGPT feature called 'adult mode'.
She has known Trae Stephens, a Founders Fund partner, for at least a decade and has been friendly with the team for years.
Beiermeister is interested in backing startups in AI infrastructure, agentic systems, defense, energy, climate, biotech, and regulated frontiers.
caption:
What happens when a top AI exec joins a major VC firm?

Ryan Beiermeister has joined Founders Fund as a partner. She previously spent about two years as VP of Product Policy at OpenAI.

Beiermeister was reportedly fired from OpenAI in February after objecting to a planned ChatGPT feature called 'adult mode'.

She has known Trae Stephens, a Founders Fund partner, for at least a decade and has been friendly with the team for years.

Beiermeister is interested in backing startups in AI infrastructure, agentic systems, defense, energy, climate, biotech, and regulated frontiers.

headline_marked: Build High-Speed Vision Analyzers on [[Android with Edge AI]]
headline: Build High-Speed Vision Analyzers on Android with Edge AI
summary: Learn to design a sophisticated pipeline for high-speed vision analysis on Android devices.
details: Building high-speed vision analyzers on Android requires a deep understanding of Edge AI and its constraints. The goal is to minimize latency-to-insight, which is the time elapsed from the moment a photon hits the camera sensor to the moment a meaningful inference result is rendered on the screen.

Modern Android System on Chips (SoCs) are heterogeneous computing powerhouses, comprising CPUs, NPUs, GPUs, and DSPs. Each component has a specific role in the vision analysis pipeline, and leveraging them effectively is crucial for high-performance vision analysis.

The NPU handles massive tensor operations, while the GPU is optimized for pre-processing. The DSP is ideal for 'Always-On' triggers and basic motion detection. By utilizing these components efficiently, developers can create high-speed vision analyzers that feel like magic.
